title: Cap. X: Superest ultima — Garissoles from imputed Christ’s justice
pass_a_gloss: There remains his last reason, drawn from the imputation of Christ's justice. He frames it thus: Whatever overturns or weakens the doctrine of imputed Christ's justice is not to be admitted or tolerated, but wholly removed and rejected. But by the dogma of Non-imputation of Adam's sin, the doctrine of the imputation of Christ's justice is certainly weakened not a little, since from denial of the former the easiest slip is to denial of the latter. For since in Christ as a second Adam we have a most certain remedy against the evils and damages brought upon the human race from the first Adam; and a remedy ought to answer in just proportion to the diseases it is prepared to heal; whoever thinks we draw from Adam no damage besides native corruption, and will set over against that corruption the gift of sanctification, will easily come to this view: that there is in us no reatus prior to our original blot on account of Adam's disobedience, and that there is no need of any imputation of Christ's justice that would precede sanctification in the order of nature — because where there is no evil, there is also no need of a remedy.
pass_b_english: His last argument remains, drawn from the imputation of Christ’s justice. He puts it this way: anything that overturns or shakes the teaching of Christ’s imputed righteousness must not be allowed or endured, but must be rooted out and cast off entirely. Yet the dogma that Adam’s sin is not imputed, he says, certainly shakes that teaching more than a little — because denying the first makes denying the second an easy slide. Since in Christ, the second Adam, we have a sure remedy against the evils and losses the first Adam brought on the human race, and a remedy ought to match the diseases it is meant to heal, anyone who thinks we inherit from Adam nothing worse than native corruption — and who sets sanctification over against that corruption — will soon conclude that we have no guilt earlier than our original stain from Adam’s disobedience, and that we need no imputation of Christ’s justice ahead of sanctification in nature’s order: where there is no evil, no remedy is needed.
source_text: Superest ultima eius ratio ducta ab imputatione Iustitiae Christi. Eam sic concipit. Quod doctrinam de imputata Christi justitia vel convellit, vel labefactat, neque admittendum, neque tolerandum est, sed amolendum omnino ac rejiciendum. Atqui dogmate de Non-imputatione peccati Adae, doctrinam de imputatione justitiae Christi, non parum labefactari certum est, cum ex negatione prioris facillimus sit lapsus ad posterioris negationem. Nam cum in Christo tanquam secundo Adamo, remedium habeamus certissimum adversus ea mala & damna, quae sunt in genus humanum a primo Adamo invecta; Remedium autem morbis, quibus sanandis paratum est, justa proportione respondere debeat; qui praeter nativam corruptionem, nihil nos damni ex Adamo trahere existimabit, & huic corruptioni considerabit ex adverso respondere donum sanctificationis, facile in eam sententiam deveniet, cum nullus sit in nobis propter Adae inobedientiam reatus labe nostra originali prior, neque opus esse ulla justitia Christi imputatione, quae sanctificationem ordine naturae praecedat: quia ubi nullum est malum, nullo etiam opus est remedio.

choices.decision: Non-imputation of Adam's sin said to shake imputed Christ's justice via remedy-proportion

notes: Cap. X Superest ultima densify section 125 from locked 1661 Latin (pp. 127–130 tip).
